questions.question: "Bell-clapper deformity" is a predisposing factor for:
questions.detail: This anomaly involves an abnormally high attachment of the tunica vaginalis, allowing the testicle to rotate freely.

questions.question: On Doppler ultrasound, which finding is the "gold standard" for diagnosing testicular torsion?
choices: Absent or markedly diminished blood flow in the testis
questions.detail: Comparison with the contralateral side is essential for confirming absent perfusion.

questions.question: A 25-year-old male presents with a painless, solid, hypoechoic testicular mass. Lab work shows elevated hCG but normal AFP. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.detail: Seminomas are the most common germ cell tumor and typically do not secrete AFP.

questions.question: Testicular cancer showing "heterogeneous" morphology with cystic areas and calcifications, associated with elevation of both hCG and AFP, is likely a:
questions.detail: NSGCTs are more aggressive and frequently secrete both markers.

questions.question: "Testicular microlithiasis" (5 or more tiny calcifications per field) requires annual follow-up if combined with which risk factor?
choices: History of cryptorchidism or personal/family history of germ cell tumor
questions.detail: While microlithiasis is often benign, it is a marker for increased cancer risk in patients with these specific histories.

questions.question: A "lamellated" or "onion-skin" appearance of a testicular mass on ultrasound is characteristic of which benign entity?
questions.detail: These benign cysts contain keratin layers that create the characteristic striated appearance.

questions.question: Which type of testicular tumor is the most common bilateral primary malignancy in men over age 60?
questions.detail: Testicular lymphoma is a systemic disease and often presents bilaterally in older men.

questions.question: A "varicocele" is a dilation of the pampiniform plexus of veins. Why is an ISOLATED right-sided varicocele clinically concerning?
choices: It may indicate a retroperitoneal mass (e.g., RCC) obstructing the right gonadal vein
It is more painful than the left
questions.detail: Because the right gonadal vein drains directly into the IVC (rather than the renal vein), an isolated right varicocele suggests an extrinsic obstruction of the IVC or vein origin.

questions.question: "Fournier gangrene" is a surgical emergency of the scrotum characterized by:
questions.detail: Identifying gas within the scrotal soft tissues on imaging is critical.

questions.question: A painless, fluid-filled mass located in the "head" of the epididymis that contains non-viable sperm is a:
questions.detail: These are common benign cystic lesions of the epididymal head.
